question.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overset{―}{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma ,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x=\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma 
$$

Substituting $x=5.4,$ $z=0.5,$ and $\sigma =2.4$ into the formula and solving for $\overset{―}{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma  \\ 5.4 & =\overset{―}{x}+0.5\cdot 2.4 \\ 5.4 & =\overset{―}{x}+1.2 \\ \overset{―}{x} & =4.2.\end{aligned}
$$
